systems.name: Planned integrated public transport network (PMA IPTN)

sources.title: Integrated Public Transport Network Faisalabad (file name: Faisalabad Integrated Feeder Routes)
Master Plan Faisalabad 2021-2041, Transportation Report, section 5.1 and Figs 5-1/5-2 (pp. 5-55 to 5-57)
sources.publisher: Faisalabad Development Authority (consultants Osmani & Co., Prof. S.N. Pollalis)

systems.notes: 35-route PMA planning network (undated PDF, c.2017-2019) in 5 phases: 16 mini-bus feeders (Ph I-II), 9 feeders (Ph III), 4 express (Ph IV), 6 sub-urban (Ph V); total 568.5 km, 459 buses. Headway is not printed (round-trip time and bus count are). Same format as lahore-iptn-planned / multan-iptn-planned. Different from the Faisalabad Metrobus Red/Orange feeder networks in the FDA Master Plan (43 + 41 routes, summary tables only).

sources.title: PMA, Rawalpindi Integrated Transportation System - Phase I, route table (image)

routes.notes: PMA Phase-I feeder plan for the Rawalpindi-Islamabad Metrobus: route 1, 9 km, 12 mini-buses (8 m). open_questions: Faisalabad: FDA Master Plan 2021-41 Transportation Report (2023, pp.5-55 to 5-57) shows the old public routes B-1, B-4, B-6, B-7, B-8, B-9, B-10, B-11, W-13, W-17, W-19, W-20, W-22, W-23 on a map only (no termini or stops), and says only B-10, B-11 and W-20 still ran in 2023. The FUTS route register is needed to model them; 11b Kotwali-Khurrianwala in faisalabad-private-wagons looks like B-11.
Faisalabad IPTN route 17 prints only one terminal ('Lower Canal Road via Humayon Town, Fakharabad'); the other end is assumed.
Faisalabad IPTN Phase-III: the route rows say Standard Bus, the summary table says Mini Bus (9 routes, 142 buses).
Rawalpindi PMA Phase-I feeder plan: undated, never launched; 'Marrir Br' / 'Murir Bridge' taken to be the Murree Road bridge at Marrir Chowk.
Peshawar: the pre-BRT inventory (7 minibus, 2 wagon, 13 Suzuki, 6 Qingqi routes per ADB EIA 2017 p.67) exists only in the undisclosed ADB PPTA inception report (Apr 2016) and CDIA PFS (2014).
Karachi: the 267-route / 12,399-permit register (KTIP Table 3-3-7, from CDGK RSOQ 2009) and the Confirmatory Green Routes Study (Exponent Engineers 2008/2010) are not online.
Quetta: GPP Balochistan intra-city bus transport study (2021-22) and QDA master plan transport plan not published; news reports about 550 private buses on 15 routes, none named.

Multan: the 2012 Master Plan cites a 2005 UET study for the Transport Department (8 bus routes / 143 buses, 12 wagon routes / 505 wagons) and an RTA franchise scheme of 6 routes / 121 buses; neither list is published. Fig 12.6 maps existing bus and wagon routes without names.
